title: Windjammers
subtitle: A flying disc across the court
summary: Windjammers is Data East's arcade sports game, first released for Neo Geo on 17 February 1994.
body: Windjammers is Data East's arcade sports game, first released for Neo Geo on 17 February 1994. Two opponents throw a flying disc across a divided court, trying to drive it into the goal behind the other player. Six competitors provide different combinations of speed, strength and special throws. The basic exchange is immediately legible: catch the disc, choose an angle and send it back. As the rally accelerates, that small sequence becomes a rapid contest of positioning, anticipation and the ability to recover before the next return reaches the goal.

Defence requires meeting the disc or diving to intercept it. Once caught, the player has only a short time to release it and cannot move while holding it, making the choice of return urgent. A throw can travel directly towards a goal or bounce from the side walls. Lofted discs display a landing target that must be reached to prevent a miss. The game keeps changing the shape of the exchange, asking the player to read a fast horizontal shot differently from an airborne disc falling into the court.

Goal sections award different points, while missing an airborne disc gives the opponent a smaller score. Each court changes the arrangement of those targets, making the arena itself part of choosing an attacking angle. Barriers can further alter a ricochet. Seiichi Hamada and Tomoyoshi Sato composed the music for the original release. Later adaptations introduced the game to new competitive audiences, and Dotemu eventually developed a sequel. The enduring attraction remains the original's compact chain of decisions, where a successful defensive catch instantly becomes the next chance to score.
